links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of professionals with versus without AI assistance for skin lesion triage
links.effect: Phase 1: sensitivity and specificity improved from 0.64 and 0.90 (without AI) to 0.80 and 0.92 (with AI), matching standalone model performance.
links.quote: In Phase 1, sensitivity and specificity improved from 0.64 and 0.90 (without AI) to 0.80 and 0.92 (with AI), matching the model's standalone performance.

links.outcome: Triage effectiveness and unnecessary referrals with AI assistance among rural community health workers in pilot
links.effect: Phase 2 (57 community health workers): AI assistance increased triage effectiveness by 17% and reduced unnecessary referrals by 30%; participant feedback positive.
links.quote: In Phase 2, with 57 community health workers in rural areas, AI assistance increased triage effectiveness by 17% and reduced unnecessary referrals by 30%.

unlisted_practices: Offline-capable mobile deployment of AI triage for low-resource rural settings
Dermatologist-developed five-level priority triage protocol embedded in AI output

screen.reason: The study evaluates the deployment of an AI-assisted mobile triage tool for generalist healthcare professionals and community health workers, comparing clinical performance (sensitivity, specificity, triage effectiveness, and referral rates) with and without the AI assistance.

primary.practice: AI-assisted triage decision support for community health workers
